Parse and serialise MIME types

Source: R/record.R
mime_parse.Rd

mime_parse() is the WHATWG MIME Sniffing Standard's "parse a MIME type": type and subtype are lower-cased HTTP tokens; parameters keep their order, names are lower-cased, quoted values are unescaped, and a repeated name keeps its first value. mime_format() is "serialize a MIME type", quoting a value that is empty or not a token.

Usage

mime_parse(x, strict = FALSE)

mime_format(record)

Arguments

x

A character vector of MIME types, such as Content-Type header values.

strict

If TRUE, an input that fails to parse raises zumime_parse_error instead of giving NULL.

record

One record from mime_parse(), or a list of them.

Value

mime_parse() returns a list with one record per input: a list of type, subtype and parameters (a named list of strings), or NULL for input that fails to parse and for NA.

mime_format() returns a character vector, NA for a NULL record.

References

https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#parsing-a-mime-type

Examples

rec <- mime_parse("Text/HTML; Charset=\"UTF-8\"; charset=latin1")
str(rec)
#> List of 1
#>  $ :List of 3
#>   ..$ type      : chr "text"
#>   ..$ subtype   : chr "html"
#>   ..$ parameters:List of 1
#>   .. ..$ charset: chr "UTF-8"
mime_format(rec)
#> [1] "text/html;charset=UTF-8"
mime_format(mime_parse("text/plain;name=\"a b\""))
#> [1] "text/plain;name=\"a b\""
mime_parse("not a type")
#> [[1]]
#> NULL
#>
